+    def widen_to_span_with_recorded_value(self, chooser):
+        """Replace a strategy's choices with a ValueHole carrying the value it
+        produced, so that the replay re-encodes that value more simply.
+
+        We look for a span which starts with a non-forced zero-based non-zero
+        integer choice (heuristically: a one_of branch selector), makes more
+        than one choice, and has a recorded value, and propose the same
+        choice sequence with the span's choices replaced by a single
+        ValueHole. At replay time the hole is claimed by whichever strategy
+        draws at that position: a one_of's ``_invert`` tries every alternative
+        in-process and returns the simplest encoding whose image contains the
+        value, so one test execution covers all of its branches. If the
+        result is a strictly simpler choice sequence which still fails, it is
+        kept, and normal shrinking takes the re-encoded value the rest of the
+        way. All knowledge of how to encode values lives with the strategies,
+        not here.
+        """
+        node = chooser.choose(
+            self.nodes,
+            lambda n: (
+                n.type == "integer"
+                and not n.was_forced
+                and n.constraints["min_value"] == 0
+                and n.value != 0
+            ),
+        )
+
+        span_idx = chooser.choose(
+            self.spans_starting_at[node.index],
+            # Single-choice spans are excluded: they are either not a one_of
+            # (e.g. the selector draw's own span), or a one_of whose current
+            # branch made no choices, like just() - and a re-encoding of the
+            # latter would be longer, which incorporate_test_data rejects.
+            lambda i: self.spans[i].recorded_value is not None
+            and self.spans[i].choice_count > 1,
+        )
+        span = self.spans[span_idx]
+
+        attempt = (
+            self.choices[: span.start]
+            + (ValueHole(span.recorded_value),)
+            + self.choices[span.end :]
+        )
+        self.incorporate_test_data(self.engine.cached_test_function(attempt))
+

+    data = ConjectureData.for_choices(choices)

+        replayed = data.draw(strategy)

+def check_roundtrip_many(strategy, data):

+def test_integers(data):

+"""Quality tests for ``wide_strategy | specific_strategy`` combinations.
+
+Each predicate below is chosen so that random draws from the wide (open)
+strategy satisfy it with probability well under 1%, so that the initial
+failing example essentially always comes from the specific branch. Note that
+these are end-to-end smoke tests, and could in principle be satisfied without
+widening - e.g. if constants discovery mined the needle from the test source
+and generated it directly in the wide branch. The authoritative evidence that
+widening itself rewrites the choice sequence is the
+test_widening_* / test_full_shrink_* tests in tests/conjecture/test_shrinker.py,
+which assert exact choice-sequence transitions.
+
+``just()`` values deliberately do not widen: a just() draw makes no choices,
+so any wide-branch encoding of its value would make the choice sequence
+longer, which the shrinker never accepts.
+"""
+
+import hypothesis.strategies as st
+from hypothesis.strategies import builds, integers, just, lists, sampled_from, text
+
+from tests.common.debug import minimal
+
+
+def test_widen_text_with_sampled_from():
+    strat = text() | sampled_from(["quetzalcoatl-1", "quetzalcoatl-2"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "quetzalcoatl" in s)
+    assert val == "quetzalcoatl"
+
+
+def test_widen_integers_with_sampled_from():
+    # A narrow window around the sampled values - random ``integers()`` draws
+    # hit it much less than 1% of the time.
+    strat = integers() | sampled_from([4991, 4999, 5001, 5009])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda n: 4990 <= n <= 5010)
+    assert val == 4990
+
+
+def test_widen_bounded_integers_with_sampled_from():
+    strat = integers(0, 10_000) | sampled_from([4991, 5009])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda n: 4990 <= n <= 5010)
+    assert val == 4990
+
+
+def test_widen_binary_with_sampled_from():
+    strat = st.binary() | sampled_from([b"xyz-abcdefghijk-one", b"xyz-abcdefghijk-two"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda b: b"abc" in b)
+    assert val == b"abc"
+
+
+def test_widen_floats_with_sampled_from():
+    # A narrow window well away from the typical shrink targets.
+    strat = st.floats() | sampled_from([11.0, 11.5])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda x: 10.0 <= x <= 12.0)
+    assert val == 10.0
+
+
+def test_widen_text_in_a_list():
+    strat = lists(text() | sampled_from(["marker-specific-string", "marker-other"]))
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda xs: any("marker" in x for x in xs))
+    assert val == ["marker"]
+
+
+def test_widen_three_way_one_of():
+    # ``quux`` is a distinctive sequence, essentially never generated by
+    # random ``text()``, so the initial failure comes from a sampled branch.
+    strat = (
+        text()
+        | sampled_from(["quux-kangaroo", "quux-wallaby"])
+        | sampled_from(["numbat-quux", "quokka-quux"])
+    )
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda v: "quux" in v)
+    assert val == "quux"
+
+
+def test_widen_text_with_builds():
+    compound = builds(
+        lambda a, b: a + " middle " + b,
+        sampled_from(["alpha", "beta"]),
+        sampled_from(["gamma", "delta"]),
+    )
+    strat = text() | compound
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "middle" in s)
+    assert val == "middle"
+
+
+# The tests below show that widening still reaches the minimum when the wide
+# strategy carries restrictions, as long as the specific branch's value
+# respects those restrictions.
+
+
+def test_widen_text_with_alphabet():
+    strat = text(alphabet="abcd") | sampled_from(["ddaabbccdddd", "ddddccbbaadd"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "aabbccdd" in s or "ddccbbaa" in s)
+    assert val == "aabbccdd"
+
+
+def test_widen_text_with_min_size():
+    strat = text(min_size=3) | sampled_from(["helloworld", "hellothere"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "hello" in s)
+    assert val == "hello"
+
+
+def test_widen_text_with_max_size():
+    # A 2-char distinctive sequence inside a 5-char cap - very rare.
+    strat = text(max_size=5) | sampled_from(["xyzzy", "xyzab"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "xy" in s)
+    assert val == "xy"
+
+
+def test_widen_integers_with_min_value():
+    strat = integers(min_value=10) | sampled_from([4991, 5009])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda n: 4990 <= n <= 5010)
+    assert val == 4990
+
+
+def test_widen_integers_with_max_value():
+    strat = integers(max_value=100) | sampled_from([-4991, -5009])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda n: -5010 <= n <= -4990)
+    assert val == -4990
+
+
+def test_widen_floats_with_range():
+    strat = st.floats(0.0, 100.0) | sampled_from([11.0, 11.5])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda x: 10.0 <= x <= 12.0)
+    assert val == 10.0
+
+
+def test_widen_binary_with_min_size():
+    strat = st.binary(min_size=3) | sampled_from([b"helloworld", b"hellothere"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda b: b"hello" in b)
+    assert val == b"hello"
+
+
+def test_widen_skips_alternatives_that_cannot_hold_the_value():
+    # booleans() can never hold these values, so widening settles on the
+    # integers() branch instead.
+    strat = st.booleans() | integers() | sampled_from([4991, 5009])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda n: 4990 <= n <= 5010)
+    assert val == 4990
+
+
+def test_just_does_not_widen():
+    # Accepted limitation: a just() span has no choices to re-encode.
+    strat = text() | just("xyzzy-plover")
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "xyzzy" in s)
+    assert val == "xyzzy-plover"
+
+
+def test_single_element_sampled_from_does_not_widen():
+    # sampled_from with one element collapses to just() at construction time,
+    # and so inherits its limitation.
+    strat = text() | sampled_from(["xyzzy-plover"])
+    val = minimal(strat, lambda s: "xyzzy" in s)
+    assert val == "xyzzy-plover"
